> I think we could insert it to the options directly, instead of using experimental, but matching legacy sampler is good enough for now.

I had similar doubts when writing the PR, and mostly prioritized compatibility with legacy sampler. As `SamplerExecutionOptions` inherits from `ExecutionOptions`, I believe the user can just use them directly already:

```python
...
options.execution.scheduler_timing = True
``` 

I ended up seeing the ability to use either that or `experimental` as a "feature" of sorts, and mostly a matter of deciding when it is released if we encourage one over the other (or if we want to avoid `experimental` and break compatibility). Happy to tweak as needed.

Since Ian pointed me at this:

Fwiw, that message was only supposed to be a first pass at our policy, and to try and make it sufficiently easy to disclose LLM use in the PR body without judgment.  Before the change, it was a complete slog trying to get people to mention what they'd used, and soem people would (I'm _pretty_ sure) just lie to us about it

For the comment:

> Any code generated by LLM or modified from LLM suggestions must commented inline too.

This _is_ intended to refer to code comments.  You guys on this repo aren't required to follow the same principles as Qiskit, but the intention behind the policy is that the licensing status of LLM-generated code is not 100% clear, so we were treating it similarly to the licensing requirements of porting/using code from another open-source codebase.  The way I wrote it to Ian is:

> rather than "Function XYZ was originally taken from `<url>` at commit `<sha1>` and used under the terms of Apache-2.0." or whatever, it's "Function XYZ was originally partially generated by LLM `<model>`."

We don't worry about it when it's trivial changes that wouldn't be copyrightable, and I won't sit here and tell you that we successfully enforce it on every PR, but that _was_ the intent.  When I'm the reviewer, I do roughly try and enforce it.

---

We were actually talking relatively recently within the Qiskit SDK that we should revisit the wording of the PR prompt, because it could be clearer, and when I wrote out those three options, I wasn't imaginative enough about how people use LLMs - the message was written a few months ago, just when the influx was starting.

btw, of the three options, the only one I _actually_ care about knowing is if they used generative AI for any of the code that made it into the patch.  The middle option about "I used it for the PR description" was there so that people who use LLMs to help write in English would have an option to tick that wasn't "I used it to generate code" and "I didn't use an LLM", without me needing to spell out in far too many words what constitutes "generated code [that I actually care about from a potential licensing problem situation]"

Thanks for the insight, Jake! This brings in more clarity into the topic, and while in this repository we are indeed at a different stage when it comes to LLM-assisted contributions (small percentage from outside contributors), with the template changes we should be in a better place for accommodating them (and make the disclosing easier and more streamline). 

For what is worth, I do like the simplicity of the template lines (thanks for those!), even if it is a first pass  - we'll be keeping an eye on how it evolves in Qiskit, as I also value staying on par to the extent possibles specially for easing contributor's life between repos.

After a more careful consideration, the suboptimality identified in this issue is known and beyond the scope of this particular piece of code. We are currently grouping once per parameter set, because in principle, each parameter set could have a different set of observables attached to it (note that issue mistakenly uses observable instead of observable set). This goes back to the broadcasting, which we already know to cause such sub-optimal performance (for example, in the calculation of expectation values, which could potentially be grouped into more efficient numpy calls, and isn't for similar reasons).

I am going to close this issue, and unless we opt to special case some specific broadcasting scenarios (mostly all-to-all), I think there is no way to improve here.

This is already done, by allowing `mcm_name` to be `measure` (before it had to start with `measure_`), and similarly for `mcr_name`. The default is to replace them both with `measure_2` and `reset_2`, and this choice of defaults is the breaking change. > The default is to replace them both with `measure_2` and `reset_2`, and this choice of defaults is the breaking change. 

I think we can either

1. Release a new pass (`ConvertToMidCircuitMeasureReset` ?) that does both `measure_2` and `reset_2`, update the existing `ConvertToMidCircuitMeasure` to just call this new pass (with `mcr_name="reset"`), and deprecate the existing pass. After the 3 months deprecation period we'd have just the new pass. 
2. Update `ConvertToMidCircuitMeasure` to include mcr, but default to `mcr_name="reset"` with a warning saying the default will change after the deprecation period. 

Option 1 is the more proper way of making a change, but it requires users to update their code. We could also do option 1 but at the end of the deprecation period, redirect `ConvertToMidCircuitMeasure` to `ConvertToMidCircuitMeasureReset` instead of dropping it. 

By the way, I don't really like the name `ConvertToMidCircuitMeasureReset`, since we may release a `measure_reset` instruction.

## Situation

Several tests cases that assert on an error message fail. Example:

```
AssertionError: Regex pattern did not match.
  Expected regex: '.*Error code (1602|6050).*'
  Actual message: "'Unable to retrieve job result. RuntimeError: Input Error:
   Rep delay 0.0021 outside of valid range 0 - 0.002 -- https://ibm.biz/error_codes#6050'"
```

The test sets `rep_delay = rep_delay_range[1] + 0.0001` (= `0.0021`, just above the
backend max of `0.002`), submits a Bell circuit, and expects `job.result()` to
raise `RuntimeJobFailureError` matching `.*Error code (1602|6050).*`.

## What actually happened

- The job **failed correctly** with error **6050** ("Rep delay 0.0021 outside of
  valid range") — exactly the condition and code the test expects.
- The correct exception type (`RuntimeJobFailureError`) **was** raised — only the
  message *regex* failed.
- The regex needs the literal substring `Error code 6050`. The service now renders
  coded errors as a URL fragment, `https://ibm.biz/error_codes#6050`, so
  `Error code 6050` no longer appears and the regex can never match.

This is a **server-side, client-agnostic message-format change**

Because the message originates server-side, it changed identically for **both**
samplers — the failure is not specific to the wrapper.

## Why this is not a wrapper defect (parity holds)

The wrapper drives the *same* server-side 6050 rejection as legacy:

- No client-side range validation: in the wrapper options model
  (`qiskit_ibm_runtime/options_models/execution_options.py:29`), `rep_delay` is a
  plain `float | None` — it is **not** checked against `rep_delay_range`.

So both samplers ship `rep_delay=0.0021` unchanged, both get the 6050 rejection,
both raise `RuntimeJobFailureError` with the same new-format message.

Thanks for spotting this!

> **Suggested solutions**
> Qiskit IBM Runtime already uses `~/.qiskit` directory to store admin data. Let's use this directory to cache data from backends.

While the `~/.qiskit` directory is indeed already being used, it is used only for credential configuration. Expanding its usage to accommodate other kind of data is not something we want to explore currently, as it has some implications and side effects (documentation, maintenance, backwards compatibility) and as it is likely to clash with longer term plans in the library related to passing secrets and configuration. So let's not increase the surface area of `~/.qiskit` instead.

`refresh()` should indeed not fail in system-wide installations, though. I do agree that modifying local installation files is not a good practice (arguably correctly documented in the documentation, but still) - instead, would you be up for solving it via updating `refresh()` with an optional parameter that causes the changes not to be persisted to disk (or to a temporary file)?

This would cause the changes not to be persisted between sessions, but would at least allow users that don't have write access to the package file to refresh their fake backends.

> `refresh()` should indeed not fail in system-wide installations, though. This does not fix the underlying bug which is the package (attempting to) modifying files under site-packages. This breaks the expectation that files there are read-only. Citing, for example, the docs of `importlib.resources`:

> Resources and packages do not have to exist as physical files and directories on the file system: for example, a package and its resources can be imported from a zip file using [zipimport](https://docs.python.org/3/library/zipimport.html#module-zipimport).

Would it be acceptable to store everything on a temporary directory (using `tempfile`) by default (instead of using `~/.qiskit`), and allow to use the current mechanism with an optional flag? In this way, at least, by default, it would not be doing something "bad".

> This does not fix the underlying bug which is the package (attempting to) modifying files under site-packages.

Might be a discussion on semantics. I see the bug as "`refresh()` does fail ungracefully when the package is installed system-wide and the user does not have write permissions".  The mechanism used by `refresh()` I do agree is questionable, but it is documented and its closer to a feature than a bug.

> Would it be acceptable to store everything on a temporary directory (using tempfile) by default (instead of using ~/.qiskit), and allow to use the current mechanism with an optional flag? In this way, at least, by default, it would not be doing something "bad".

Unfortunately that would be a backwards-incompatible change - and having the changes persist between sessions (even if using a "creative" mechanism) in regular use cases is a feature that we want to maintain. Having the optional flag (not as the default behavior) at least allows user to use `refresh()` during the session, bringing it closer to the `IBMBackend.refresh()` spirit ("Retrieve the newest backend configuration and refresh the current backend target.") - it sacrifices persistence, but hopefully covers the scenario up to some decent extent.

Depending on the use case, it might also make sense to solve it / sweeten it in user-land (subclassing `FakeBackendV2` / `FakeProviderForBackendV2` or generating backends with a custom path for their filenames as needed)?

Okay, then I will modify the PR to add an optional flag to store the retrieved data in a temp folder. By default, nothing will change. When that flag is set, `refresh()` does not attempt to modify the files in site-packages at the cost of not having the changes persist over time.

By the way, this feature that changes are permanent also breaks other expectations in Qiskit. For example, that fixing all the transpiler and sampler seeds will produce reproducible results on fake providers with fixed versions of Qiskit and Qiskit IBM Runtime. This breaks as soon as `refresh()` is used.

Hi @TsafrirA, the intention of wanting millisecond resolution execution times is performance monitoring and profiling. ExecutionSpans are second resolution, so not really useful. In addition, the documentation of ExecutionSpan (public API documentation v0.47.0) explictily states that no guarantee is made that the start and stop time of the span are close to the start and stop time of the PUB. Therefore they can hardly be used to compare the execution times of circuit variants.

> The guarantee being made is that the referenced data definitely occurred in the reported execution span, but not necessarily that the limits of the time window are as tight as possible.
